A seat is one lookout tower on a listed ridge. The applicant files coordinates, a permit and its alidade azimuth table, plumb bob on a thread. Ten dawn readings a season arrive, bearings to six named peaks, and the node compares them with those filed by the two nearest towers, since three sight lines should meet on one summit. A ridge or permit already seated is refused.

Kit 4,200 dollars, theodolite 1,800, permit 600, road cut 9,000, so 15,600 a clone and 780,000 for fifty before any horizon is read. Two towers aimed at one peak agree on its bearing or one lies about where it stands.
